title: A gather the compiler can prove
starter:
%d   = buffer 4 dtype=i32 slot=0 data=[10 20 30 40]
%ix  = buffer 1 dtype=i32 slot=1 data=[2]
%res = buffer 1 dtype=i32 slot=2
# res[0] = d[i], where i comes from ix[0]. A negative i reads d[0];
# any other i reads d[i mod 4]. The view must be provably in bounds.
%i0  = shrink %ix 0 shape=[]
%i   = load %i0
%src = shrink %d %i shape=[]
%v   = load %src
%r0  = shrink %res 0 shape=[]
%s   = store %r0 %v
%r1  = after %res %s
hints: The starter is invalid: `%i` is loaded from memory, so its interval is all of i32, and the compiler can't prove `shrink %d %i` is inside `%d`.
Two ops shape the interval: `max %i 0` cuts off the negative half, then `mod` by 4 brings it down to `[0, 3]`.
Order matters. `mod %i 4` alone is `[-3, 3]` (the sign follows `%i`), which can still be negative. Do the `max` first.
explain: `max %i 0` has bounds `[0, INT_MAX]`, and `mod` by 4 of a value that's never negative has bounds `[0, 3]`, so `shrink %d %k shape=[]` is provably inside 4 elements. It also gives the asked-for behavior: negative indices read d[0], and big ones wrap mod 4.
